findings.title: Standalone boundary diagnostics expose the host home path
findings.trigger: Run --verify-boundary with a valid review image but a missing host Codex auth.json.
findings.execution_path: main → verify_boundary_main → verify_isolation_boundary → prepare_codex_home. The missing-file exception includes host_auth_path, becomes a boundary reason, and is printed after replacing only scratch-directory paths.
findings.consequence: The JSON intended for recorded boundary evidence contains the owner's absolute home and credential-file path. Publishing that diagnostic exposes local identity/path information contrary to the phase's redaction requirement. Credential contents are not disclosed by this reproduction.
findings.evidence: Mocked missing-auth fault injection returned exit 3 and printed: Codex sign-in file not found: /Users/review-owner/.codex/auth.json. The standalone regression test checks scratch-path replacement only; regular-review redaction tests do not exercise this entry point.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the shared home/repository/temp-path redaction to standalone public boundary output before printing. Add a standalone missing-auth regression using a synthetic home outside the scratch directory and assert that the absolute home path is absent.
